title: Text Preprocessing
description: Learn how raw text is cleaned, split into tokens and reduced to common word forms.
content:
Raw text is noisy and unstructured, so classic NLP begins with preprocessing.

**Text normalization** standardizes the input: lowercasing, punctuation handling, number normalization and spelling correction. **Tokenization** then splits text into **tokens** (words, subwords or punctuation) and sentences (**sentence segmentation**). Naive whitespace splitting fails on real cases: 'don't' merges a clitic with a word, 'New York' splits one entity, hyphenated compounds break apart, and languages written without spaces (e.g., Chinese) require a **maximum matching** algorithm that greedily extracts the longest dictionary word at each position.

**Stop words** - extremely frequent function words like 'the' and 'of' - are often removed for information retrieval to shrink the index, but this can destroy meaning in tasks sensitive to negation ('not good') or auxiliary verbs.

**Stemming** and **lemmatization** both reduce word forms to a common base. A **stemmer** applies crude suffix-stripping rules: fast and resource-light, but it may produce non-words ('studies' -> 'studi', 'flies' -> 'fli'). A **lemmatizer** uses a vocabulary plus morphological analysis to return a valid dictionary form - the **lemma** ('studies' -> 'study', 'went' -> 'go') - more accurate but slower and dependent on lexical resources.

> A typical preprocessing pipeline:
> • Normalize (casing, punctuation, numbers)
> • Tokenize into words and sentences
> • Optionally remove stop words
> • Reduce forms via stemming or lemmatization
